US rule: Creditor may not impose a Military Annual Percentage Rate (MAPR, includes most fees and add-on products) above **36%** on consumer credit to covered service members and dependants. eCFR text current to 11/09/2026.
citation: 32 CFR 232.4(b), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-32/subtitle-A/chapter-I/subchapter-O/part-232/section-232.4

US rule: Licensed finance lender may charge at most **36% simple annual interest + the Federal Funds Rate** (H.15, first day of prior month). Minimum term 12 months; free credit-education offer required. Added by AB 539 (eff. 1 Jan 2020). SB 825 (2025) would amend section: enactment status not confirmed (verify).
citation: Cal. Fin. Code §22304.5; DFPI notice https://dfpi.ca.gov/regulated-industries/important-notices/new-requirements-for-licensees-making-consumer-loans-of-2500-to-10000-california-financing-law/

parameter: CFPB supervision: auto finance larger participants
US rule: Non-bank auto lenders with **≥10,000 aggregate annual originations** (with affiliates, prior calendar year) are "larger participants" subject to CFPB supervision. Aug-2025 CFPB notice floated raising the threshold to 300,000-1,050,000; no final rule found (verify).
citation: 12 CFR 1090.108, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-X/part-1090/subpart-B/section-1090.108 ; 90 FR (8 Aug 2025) https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-08-08/html/2025-15089.htm

US rule: One-month pawn loans, max APR by bracket (1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027): **240%** to $276; **180%** $276.01-$1,840; **30%** $1,840.01-$2,760; **12%** $2,760.01-$23,000. Max amount financed ceiling $23,000. Any service charge above $15 is refundable pro-rata on early payoff.
citation: Tex. Fin. Code §371.158-.159; OCCC rate chart https://occc.texas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/PawnRateChart2027.pdf

US rule: **Vacated** by the US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit on 27 Jan 2025 (procedural: no ANPRM). Not in force. Merits not decided.
citation: NADA v. FTC (5th Cir. 2025); summary https://www.autoremarketing.com/subprime/us-court-of-appeals-vacates-cars-rule/

US rule: Underwriting (ability-to-repay) parts rescinded 2020. **Payment provisions in force since 30 Mar 2025**: after 2 failed consecutive payment withdrawals, lender must stop and get new authorisation; advance notice of unusual withdrawals. CFPB said it would not prioritise enforcement. CFPB 2026 agenda plans an NPRM to reconsider the remaining provisions.
citation: 12 CFR 1041.7-.9; https://infobytes.orrick.com/2025-01-17/cfpb-announces-march-30-compliance-date-for-payday-lending-rule/ ; https://www.sheppard.com/insights/blogs/cfpbs-2026-regulatory-agenda-tees-up-long-awaited-nprm-to-reconsider-payday-lending-rule

US rule: Pawn service charge (incl. 2% interest) max **25% of amount financed per 30-day period**, minimum $5. Maturity **30 days**; parties may extend. Unredeemed goods must be held **30 more days after maturity**; then **automatically forfeited**, title vests in pawnbroker, no recourse against the borrower beyond the goods. 2025 law (ch. 2025-33, SB 678) changed forms/recordkeeping, not the caps (verify against 2026 text).
citation: Fla. Stat. §539.001 (FindLaw text "current as of 1 Jan 2025") https://codes.findlaw.com/fl/title-xxxiii-regulation-of-trade-commerce-investments-and-solicitations/fl-st-sect-539-001/ ; https://laws.flrules.org/2025/33

CFPB small-dollar (payday) rule does **not** cover traditional possessory, non-recourse pawn loans. MLA **does** cover pawn loans (36% MAPR).

US rule: Term usually 30-90 days + grace period 14-90 days; fees **4%-25% per month** as state law allows; on default the item is forfeited to the lender and moved to inventory at loan principal. Non-recourse: no credit-bureau hit or collections. State law sets fees, holding periods before sale, and do-not-buy / police database checks.
citation: FirstCash 10-K FY2025, filed 9 Feb 2026 (link above)

US rule: Banks can "export" home-state rates (state banks via DIDMCA §521, 12 USC 1831d). A non-bank cannot, unless it partners with a bank, which invites "true lender" challenges. States can **opt out** of DIDMCA §521 (Colorado did). 10th Cir. panel (10 Nov 2025) upheld Colorado's broad opt-out; **en banc rehearing granted 2 Apr 2026**, panel opinion vacated, district-court injunction (blocking the opt-out for out-of-state state banks) back in force; no en banc decision found as of 2026-11-13. More states (NY, RI, WI, OR) have bills.
citation: NAIB v. Weiser, No. 24-1293 (10th Cir.); CRS Legal Sidebar LSB11433 (22 May 2026) https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/LSB11433.html ; https://www.consumerfinancemonitor.com/2026/04/02/tenth-circuit-grants-rehearing-en-banc-in-colorado-opt-out-litigation/

US rule: A non-bank consumer lender needs a **state licence in each state** where it lends; most states now file and renew through **NMLS**. Example Texas "Regulated Lender" licence (Ch. 342): moved to NMLS from 15 Jul 2025; **$25,000 net assets per licensed location**, criminal background check of principals, finance experience, audited or bank-confirmed financials; fees $200 application + $600 licence + $25 NMLS. Example Wyoming: consumer lender licence filed via NMLS, renewed yearly Nov-Dec. Contrast with banks: banks hold a federal (OCC) or state charter, are deposit-insured, and can export home-state rates.
citation: TX OCCC Regulated Lender Branch checklist (updated 23 Jan 2026) https://occc.texas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/REG_Branch_Checklist_Jan2026.pdf ; 7 TAC §83.302(j); Wyoming https://wyomingbankingdivision.wyo.gov/consumer-lending/license-and-registration ; OneMain 10-K FY2025 (state licensing, 48 states) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1584207/000158420726000008/omf-20251231.htm

US rule: Caps are **state by state**. NCLC (Dec 2025): for a $500 6-month loan, **45 states + DC** cap the APR (median **39.5%**); for a $2,000 2-year loan, **43 states + DC** (median **34%**). Six states only bar "unconscionable" terms; Delaware and Missouri have no limit. 36% is the common benchmark cap. Mississippi Credit Availability Act (allows >300% APR) sunset moved to 1 Jul 2030. No 2026 edition found.
citation: NCLC "Predatory Installment Lending in the States 2025" https://www.nclc.org/resources/predatory-installment-lending-in-the-states-2025/ ; fact sheet https://www.nclc.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/202512_Fact-Sheet_APR-Caps-for-Installment-Loans.pdf

US rule: Dodd-Frank §1029 bars CFPB authority over car dealers **mainly selling/servicing/leasing** cars, **except** a dealer line of business that gives retail credit **directly** to consumers **and does not routinely assign** the contracts to an unaffiliated finance company (= BHPH). So BHPH lending stays within CFPB enforcement reach. CFPB larger-participant rule excludes dealers covered by §1029 from supervision (BHPH dealers are not "larger participants"); FTC keeps rule-making power over dealers.
citation: 12 U.S.C. 5519(a),(b)(2),(d) (GPO text) https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/12/5519 ; 12 CFR 1090.108(c); CFPB auto exam procedures (Aug 2019) https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/201908_cfpb_automobile-finance-examination-procedures.pdf

US rule: CFPB may act against **unfair, deceptive, or abusive** acts by any covered person (incl. non-bank lenders). "Unfair" = substantial injury, not reasonably avoidable, not outweighed by benefits. "Abusive" = interferes with understanding, or takes unreasonable advantage of lack of understanding / inability to protect self / reliance. FTC Act §5 also applies to non-banks.
citation: 12 U.S.C. 5531(a),(c),(d); 5536 https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/12/5531

US rule: Cost-of-credit disclosures (APR, finance charge, amount financed, payment schedule) at application, account opening and consummation; applies to non-bank lenders, incl. pawn (see PAWN-TILA).
citation: 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.; 12 CFR 1026; FirstCash 10-K FY2025 Government Regulation

US rule: Applicants may be judged only on factors tied to creditworthiness; no discrimination on protected grounds; adverse-action notices. Applies to all creditors.
citation: 15 U.S.C. 1691; 12 CFR 1002; FirstCash 10-K FY2025 Government Regulation

US rule: Consumer reports only for a permissible purpose; adverse-action and risk-based pricing notices; furnisher accuracy duties when reporting to bureaus.
citation: 15 U.S.C. 1681; 12 CFR 1022; FirstCash 10-K FY2025 Government Regulation

US rule: Applies to **third-party** debt collectors. A lender collecting **its own** debts **in its own name** is generally not a "debt collector"; it becomes one if it uses another name. First-party collection is still covered by UDAAP and state collection laws. eCFR text current to 11/09/2026.
citation: 12 CFR 1006.2(i) https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-X/part-1006/subpart-A/section-1006.2

US rule: State regulators (licence exams). CFPB supervises non-banks only if they are larger participants (e.g. auto ≥10,000 originations), payday/mortgage/student lenders, or by order. **OneMain** is CFPB-supervised as an auto-finance larger participant; since 2023 the supervision covers its whole consumer finance business.
citation: OneMain 10-K FY2025 (Regulation) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1584207/000158420726000008/omf-20251231.htm ; 12 CFR 1090.108

US rule: **No federal regulatory capital ratio** for non-bank consumer lenders (no Basel/CET1). Only state licence **net-worth / net-asset** minimums (e.g. Texas $25,000 per location) and surety bonds. Leverage is set by lenders' debt covenants and rating agencies. Funding = securitisations (5% risk retention applies), warehouse/VFN facilities, unsecured notes. Contrast: Ally is a bank holding company and reports CET1 **10.2%** (Q3 2026).
citation: OneMain 10-K FY2025 ("state regulatory capital requirements"; securitisation, unsecured notes; 5% risk retention); TX checklist above; Ally 8-K Ex. 99.1 Q3 2026 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040729/000119312526425698/d116845dex991.htm
